subject: Request: temporary p95 carve-out for hosted API during burst window (GlacialAI)
messages:
From: Andrew Song <andrew@glacial.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@glacial.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API p95 visibility / temporary carve-out request

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

We're getting close to production for GlacialAI's user-facing inference and have a question about the Hosted API SLOs. Our telemetry shows predictable short-duration spikes during end-of-month batch jobs and a consistent peak window (approx 20:00–22:00 UTC) where p95 jumps by ~25-40% for ~10-30 minutes.

We need a 90-day temporary allowance so our contract can move forward: specifically a p95 allowance up to 320ms during those burst windows while we implement prefix caching and a split-traffic fallback. Outside of that 30-minute rolling window, we expect to meet your standard p95 of 250ms and p50 of 35ms.

Can Redwood provide an exception (with measurable rollback conditions) and a short addendum? Procurement is on this thread for review.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Song
Head of SRE, GlacialAI

Attachments: latency-sample-traces-2026-04-02.zip (traces, 4.3MB)

Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 visibility / temporary carve-out request

Thanks for the note, Andrew — looping in Karthik and Jonas to coordinate an internal proposal.

Marissa: can you draft a one-page exception proposal with the following items?
- precise carve-out window definition (rolling 30-min window vs fixed clock window)
- temporary p95 threshold and expirations (90 days + metrics-driven rollback)
- required mitigations (prefix/KV cache plan, fallback to quantized variant)
- acceptance criteria and telemetry dashboards to be shared with the customer

Karthik/Jonas: any immediate red flags on risk or mechanics? I want something we can push to procurement by early next week.

Priyom
Head of Sales Ops (Host API customers)
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 visibility / temporary carve-out request

Ack'd — drafting now. Initial thinking below (will formalize into PDF):

Proposal summary:
- Measurement windows: rolling 30-minute window for peak detection; 6-hour rolling window for SLO aggregation/alerting.
- Temporary p95 allowance: up to 320ms during detected burst windows (defined as >20% above baseline p95 for >=5 consecutive minutes).
- Baseline targets remain: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 250ms outside carve-outs.
- Duration: 90 days with a required mitigation checkpoint at Day 30 and Day 60 (ops report + traces).
- Rollback & escalation: automatic canary (10% traffic) to fallback variant if >3 breach events in a rolling 7-day period.

I'll attach the draft and include a sample acceptance checklist for procurement.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Quick commercial / risk note from sales:

I support a timeboxed 90-day carve-out if we (a) require an ops remediation plan, (b) add explicit rollback gates, and (c) reduce our exposure by limiting the carve-out to "detected burst windows" rather than a blanket SLA change. Proposed concrete terms to offer to GlacialAI:
- Measurement: p50 (whole-day) target = 40ms; p95 measured using 6-hour rolling aggregation except when a 30-min burst window is detected.
- Carve-out: During a detected burst window (rolling 30-min), p95 budget increases to 320ms (temporary). Outside that window standard p95 250ms applies.
- Canary + fallback: enable a 10% canary routed to quantized-variant with a 200ms latency improvement estimate; if canary experiences >2 breach events in 7 days, auto-fallback and pause carve-out.
- Commercial: require a clause that makes the exception temporary and revocable on performance regressions; link to credit schedule (partial service credit if we miss post-carve-out commitments).

I'll add a short paragraph summarizing commercial credits for procurement.

Karthik
VP, Sales

Subject: Technical note: telemetry + fallback options for GlacialAI carve-out

Attaching the traces Andrew sent and a short lab-run showing the fallback variant latency profile. Key technical clarifications:
- Detection: we'll use rolling 30-minute windows with a 5-minute sliding step for burst detection to reduce false positives.
- Measurement: official SLO reporting will use a 6-hour rolling aggregation for p95 to smooth transient noise while still capturing regressions.
- Fallback: quantized variant yields ~180–210ms p95 in our microbench; on heavy KV-cache misses it still holds ~15–25% improvement.
- Mitigations: implement prefix caching, tighter KV cache eviction tuning, and an ops playbook (page 3) for incident runbooks.

Andrew / Glacial procurement team,

Thanks for the sample traces and the patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is a single-page exception addendum (slo-exception-proposal-GlacialAI.pdf) that captures the agreed technical and commercial gates. Highlights:

- Measurement windows:
  * Burst detection: rolling 30-minute window with 5-minute slide.
  * SLO reporting: 6-hour rolling aggregation (p50/p95).
- Targets:
  * Baseline (outside carve-out): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 250ms.
  * Carve-out (during detected burst windows): p95 <= 320ms (temporary; not a permanent SLA change).
- Duration & checkpoints: 90 days total; mandatory operational review at Day 30 and Day 60 with shared dashboards and traces.
- Rollback gates: if carve-out sees >3 breach events in any 7-day window (post-detection), we will pause the carve-out and route 10% traffic to fallback variant while ops remediate.
- Credits & revocation: partial credit schedule included in the addendum if commitments are missed after the 90-day window.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached addendum. If acceptable, reply with approval and we will send a DocuSign for signature.
2) If procurement prefers language edits, mark them in the PDF and we'll iterate.

DocuSign link will be generated once we have a green light.

Best,
